assumptions: The revision preserves the published ordinary1911 Backgammon interpretation and all non-correction dimensions and functions.
Bar top24→28 replaces removed crest height to preserve overall Sun190×190×28; its dependent hit radius changes to preserve80mm displacement.
Rounded profiles and recessed pips are original correction geometry; exact current checks and unprimed review remain required.
No physical print, stack handling, durability, statistically fair dice or human playtesting is claimed.

concept.interaction: Two players each own15 single-tail or split-tail drops and use cup_1 and cup_2 to roll the shared die_1 and die_2. They move opposite ways around the Sun, hit single opposing drops onto its exposed circular central bar, enter barred drops before other moves, and drain all15 beside their six-point home bank to win. All35 components retain the ordinary1911 Backgammon functions. The legal signature6,2 roll shows its six-point first submove: one attacker replaces a lone split-tail at the near rim and the victim lifts80 mm to the exposed flare. Historical opening choices, whole-throw use, doubles, touch laws,1/2/3 results and series starts remain binding as detailed in RULES.md.
concept.print_stance: All35 parts retain flat-bottom printing; cups open upward. Dice contain CAD-positioned recessed pips to be filled with dark paint; user never locates or draws pips. Sun deck16 and unobstructed round bar top28. Game-state stacks can exceed the individual Sun envelope.
risks: Smooth tail profiles require exact innermost lane clearance and2mm load-carrying tail/branch thickness.
Short bifurcated tail must read as flowing matter without animal ears or a deep fork; fresh blind review is required.
Dark recessed die face colors must survive exact CAD rendering; no blank cube or graphic-only substitute.
Recess and paint mass distribution does not establish printed dice fairness.
concept.signature_decision: Exact fixed-camera before/after states retain the legal six-point hit: attacker replaces a lone split-tail drop near the rim and victim is lifted80mm onto an open circular solar bar. Close-ups expose flowing rounded checker silhouettes and dark recessed dice pips.
concept.summary: Backgammon — coronal-rain theme: rival streams of condensed plasma travel magnetic lanes, scatter lone drops, and rain back into the Sun.
concept.title: Rainward Flow

astronomy_sources.claim: Cooling plasma follows magnetic structures and can switch paths via reconnection; competitive plugs,hits and scoring remain an analogy, not a simulation.

closest_collisions.difference: Lunar phases on conventional luxury board; here original radial plasma lanes, exposed reheating and drainage.
Circular board alone already exists; no downloaded geometry incorporated. Rainward Sun uses original35-part coronal circulation system.

research.novelty_claim: An unusual original combination; bounded search cannot prove universal novelty.

period_clarification.claim: 1909 primary text explicitly rerolls tied starts and contests starts after gammon or backgammon, corroborating abbreviated1911 wording. Its divergent quadruple-scoring option is rejected.

popularity_sources.claim: 2021 federation article reports millions playing at home and digitally.
Independent Strong Museum collection record describes ongoing popularity and play in nearly every country.

revision_baseline.treatment: Immutable reference; historical reports are not current proof.

rights_sources.claim: Penn identifies1911 as the last complete revision fully in US public domain; indexed full statement recovered after direct-fetch timeout.
Game methods differ from protectable prose and artwork; all new expression is original.

research.rules_equivalence: Every explicitly stated ordinary1911 rule preserved. Abbreviated opening and restart cases transparently interpreted with historical corroboration. No added powers,events,currencies,probability changes or modern cube.

rules_source.claim: Frozen ordinary rules, opening choices, touch laws, bearing,1/2/3 scoring and series starts; source omissions explicitly identified in RULES.md.
rules_source.rights: Public-domain historical edition; original paraphrase only.

research.source_game: Ordinary two-player Backgammon, Encyclopaedia Britannica11th edition1911; Russian variant excluded
